name: Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders): relief distributions and search and rescue
beneficiaries_note: Our build: relief distributions to displaced families; the countries the build's rows name (DRC, Sudan, South Sudan) share equally (a judgment).
summary: Besides medical care, Médecins Sans Frontières hands out relief items (shelter material, blankets, jerrycans, cooking and hygiene kits, mosquito nets) to displaced families, 653,300 families in 2025, and runs search and rescue in the Mediterranean. This model values the distributions as goods on the site's income scale plus a small share of displaced people's excess deaths averted, and the search and rescue programme (no full-year rescue count for 2025: the new ship sailed only in November) by the site's lifeboat model. The result is mostly uncertainty: MSF doesn't publish what the distributions cost (our estimate) and no study measures how many deaths household items avert.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Programmes with no outcome data
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for a programme that publishes no outcome data at all: it is valued at the result per dollar of the same kind of work elsewhere on the site, read live, and counts less by the shared slider "How much we count a programme we could only estimate from similar ones" (docs/normalization.md 2.12). A programme with some outcome data is modelled from it in the chain above, with wide ranges, never here.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Families receiving relief item distributions, 2025
rows.explainer: Families who got MSF's relief items (shelter material, blankets, mats, jerrycans, cooking sets, hygiene kits, mosquito nets) in 2025, MSF's count.

rows.label: Cost of a family's relief-item distribution, items and delivery (euros)
rows.explainer: MSF doesn't split its spending by activity or publish kit prices, so the relief distributions' cost is the families reached times a cost per family, our judgment: 45 euros. The public anchor is UK for UNHCR's family emergency survival kit (mosquito nets, jerrycans, buckets, sanitary pads, blankets, solar lamps) at £65, about 76 euros (https://shop.unrefugees.org.uk/products/emergency-survival-kit), a donor gift price for a full kit; MSF's average is lower because many of its distributions are hygiene or water kits only and it buys in bulk through MSF Supply, though transport and staff in insecure areas add to it. Low end a hygiene kit only; high end the full UNHCR kit with delivery. About 2% of programme spending at the best guess.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled programmes, including overhead
People per family
rows.explainer: The site's figure for the DRC (DHS), where MSF's largest displacement responses were in 2025; Sudan's and South Sudan's displaced families are of similar size.

rows.label: People in the families reached, 2025
Cost per person reached
rows.explainer: Context: about 12 dollars a person.

rows.label: Death rate among displaced people when the items are handed out
rows.explainer: MSF distributes to newly displaced people (eastern DRC, Sudan, Gaza, South Sudan). Mortality surveys there run above the Sphere emergency threshold of 1 death per 10,000 people a day (0.0365 a year), which is a check, not a measurement: MSF's own retrospective survey in Zamzam camp, North Darfur (January 2024, 400 households; https://www.msf.org.za/news-and-resources/news-and-resources/sudan-alarming-death-rates-and-malnutrition-crisis-north), found 2.5 per 10,000 a day (0.091 a year). Not every family reached is in a camp that bad, so our judgment is 1.5 per 10,000 a day (0.055), with Sphere's threshold as the low end and Zamzam's rate near the high.

rows.label: Death rate in the same population before the crisis
rows.explainer: The DRC's crude death rate (UN WPP via the World Bank), so only excess deaths count.

rows.label: Share of the excess deaths the items avert among the people reached
rows.explainer: No study measures the effect of household kits on mortality, so we build it from parts. Nets are the item with a measured effect: they cut all-cause child mortality by about a sixth where malaria is common (Cochrane, Pryce et al. 2018). If half the kits include a net, a third of nets are used in camp conditions for the months counted, and a fifth of the excess deaths are of young children in malaria areas, nets avert roughly 0.5 × 0.33 × 0.17 × (a share of the excess deaths they can touch), about 0.5-1% of the excess deaths; shelter, blankets, jerrycans and soap against exposure and diarrhoea perhaps as much again. Our judgment, 1.5%: zero at the low end, 4% if usage is high.

rows.label: Years the items protect a family
rows.explainer: Blankets, sheeting and jerrycans last months in camp conditions; nets a year or more. Our judgment, half a year.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the months covered, times the share the items avert.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: In displacement crises roughly 40-60% of excess deaths are of children under five (mortality surveys of camps); malaria and diarrhoea, the causes items touch, are concentrated in young children. Our judgment.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: Our judgment from the young age structure of displaced populations.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: Adults who die of exposure and disease in camps are disproportionately older; our judgment, half under 50.

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Malaria episodes averted by nets, diarrhoea by jerrycans and soap, respiratory illness by shelter and blankets: small per person. Our judgment, 0.0005 DALYs (a few illness-days a year).

rows.label: Market value of the items as a share of MSF's full cost of delivering them
rows.explainer: Transport, storage, staff and security in hard-to-reach places add to the items' price; recipients value in-kind items at or a little below their market price. Our judgment, 70%, so the value is tied to the cost (above) rather than ranged separately.

rows.label: Market value of the items a family receives (US$, 2025)
rows.explainer: About 36 dollars at the best guesses: blankets, mats, a jerrycan, a cooking set, soap and often a net or tarpaulin.

rows.label: Goods delivered per person (US$)
rows.explainer: The share of the value not counted as deaths or illness averted is small, so the whole market value counts here as goods.

rows.label: US prices: 2017 relative to 2025
rows.explainer: Puts 2025 dollars into the 2017 prices of the PPP factor and the consumption baseline.

rows.label: PPP conversion (2017 international $ per US $)
rows.explainer: The DRC's 2017 household-consumption PPP over its exchange rate (World Bank), standing in for all the countries where MSF distributes (the DRC is the largest; MSF doesn't publish the split).

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of the people reached (2017 PPP $)
rows.explainer: Displaced families in the DRC and Sudan live below the World Bank's extreme poverty line ($2.15 a day, $785 a year in 2017 PPP); the DRC's average poor person consumes about $1.5 a day. Our judgment, $550 a year.

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.explainer: A year's goods on the site's one log-income scale.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment for the goods' value
rows.explainer: The goods are valued at their market price on the site's log-income scale, which needs no study; the low end if recipients value in-kind items below market price (some resale at a discount).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment for the deaths and illness averted
rows.explainer: The deaths and illness averted rest on no study of kits, only on the nets' trial effect carried to camp conditions. Our judgment, 0.5, as for an untested health effect.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (deaths_averted_per_person * value_per_death * deaths_evidence_adj + ln_gain_per_person * $uov_per_ln_consumption * goods_evidence_adj) / (deaths_averted_per_person * value_per_death + ln_gain_per_person * $uov_per_ln_consumption)
rows.explainer: The goods and the deaths branches each apply their own evidence adjustment; this is their weighted average, for reading only.

rows.label: Share of the outcome other responders wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: OCHA's Financial Tracking Service shows the 2025 shelter and non-food-item clusters funded at 20.8% of requirements in the DRC ($27.7M of $133.4M, plan 1261), 23.9% in Sudan ($54.7M of $229.4M, plan 1220) and 33.8% in South Sudan ($15.7M of $46.5M, plan 1223; https://api.hpc.tools/v1/public/fts/flow?planId=1261&groupby=cluster, retrieved 2026-11-03). So others met roughly a quarter of the planned need, weighted towards the DRC: 1 - 0.24 = 0.76, times about 0.95 for responders outside the appeals (ICRC, governments, diaspora and host communities). Our judgment, 72%.

rows.label: MSF's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: MSF buys and delivers its own kits, sometimes with items from UNICEF or IOM pipelines. Our judgment, 95%.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: MSF's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment: items received and used as intended
rows.explainer: Some items are sold, lost in further displacement or go to families counted twice. Our judgment, 85%.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: As for MSF's medical work: almost no government money, so none displaced or pulled in; others holding back is in the counterfactual. Our judgment, 1.

rows.label: Years a gift waits before it is spent

source.title: MSF International Financial Report 2025 (combined, audited, year to 31 December 2025)
source.quote: As of year-end 2025, liquid reserves represent the equivalent of 6.0 months of the year’ s expenses

rows.explainer: Unspent funds over yearly spending: MSF's liquid reserves are 6.0 months of spending (equity reserves 7.7 months), so 0.5 years, as in MSF's medical model.

rows.label: Delay from spending to the items handed out
rows.explainer: MSF pre-positions kits in regional warehouses and buys some months ahead; our judgment, about a month.

rows.label: Middle of the months the items protect
rows.explainer: The benefits come over the months the items last, so they are discounted from the middle.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the benefits
rows.explainer: Every wait is discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit.

rows.label: Adjustments applied to both branches
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments both branches share; each applies its own evidence adjustment.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Benefits: dignity and protection (sheeting and lighting reduce assaults), cash saved for food (+5%). Harms: market disruption is negligible at this scale. Net +5%.

rows.label: Spending on programmes with no outcome data: search and rescue at sea, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: MSF's Mediterranean search and rescue: its ship Geo Barents stopped in December 2024 and the new Oyvon started only in November 2025; MSF publishes no count of people rescued in 2025 beyond a first mission's 27 people, too little to build a chain on, so it is valued by the proxy step.

rows.label: Result per dollar of comparable programmes on the site (units of value per dollar you give)
rows.explainer: The one model of rescue at sea on the site, read live: SoGive's model of the RNLI's lifeboats. The nearest evaluated programme; MSF's rescues are of migrants in distress far offshore, where each rescue may save more lives than a coastal lifeboat call-out, and the missing-data slider covers the difference.

rows.label: Share of the programme spending here that has no outcome data
rows.explainer: The modelled programmes' result counts for the rest of the spending.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give, from programmes with no outcome data
